title: Isolation of Cellular Lipid Droplets: Two Purification Techniques Starting from Yeast Cells and Human Placentas
protocol: Prepare the YE5S media by combining 36 g of YE5S powder per liter of dH2O in glass bottles or culture flasks.
Autoclave the prepared media at 121 °C for 20 min.
Allow the autoclaved media to cool to room temperature.
Transfer 10-20 ml of cooled YE5S media into a 250 ml culture flask using sterile techniques.
Inoculate the media in the culture flask with yeast cells from an agar plate using a sterile wooden stick or equivalent.
Grow yeast cells to the desired optical density at 30 °C.
Measure the optical density of the grown yeast at 595 nm using a spectrophotometer.
Transfer remaining prepared YE5S media into 2.8 L flasks, not exceeding 1 L per flask.
Introduce inoculated yeast cells from step 1.2 into each 2.8 L flask containing 1 L of YE5S media.
Grow cells to desired density at 30 °C.
Ensure cells contain lipid droplets.
Reserve 1 ml of the cell culture.
Measure optical density (O.D.) of the sample.
Add 0.1 ml of a 100 mM BODIPY 493/503 stock solution in ethanol per O.D. unit to the sample.
Place 3 μl of the labeled sample between a glass slide and cover slip.
Visualize under fluorescent microscope with GFP filter.
Pellet cells at 4 °C at 3,800 x g for 10 min.
Pour off YE5S media and wash cells with EMM + 600 mM sorbitol buffer.
Transfer washed cells to a sterile 50 ml centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge cells at 4 °C at 2,000 x g for 10 min.
Remove supernatant from the pelleted cells.
Weigh wet cell pellet.
Resuspend cells in 2 ml of EMM + 600 mM sorbitol buffer per gram of cells.
Add 5 mg each of yeast lytic enzyme and yeast lysing enzymes (Trichoderma harzianum) per gram of wet cells.
Incubate cells at 30 °C under gentle shaking at 100 rpm for 60 min.
Check lipid droplets in spheroplasts by repeating step with visualization.
Pellet spheroplasts by centrifugation at 4 °C at 2,000 x g for 5 min.
Carefully remove the supernatant using a plastic transfer pipette.
Gently resuspend the pelleted spheroplasts with ice cold 10 mM Tris-HCl, 600 mM sorbitol, and 200 μM EDTA.
Pellet the spheroplasts again using the same settings as in step 3.1.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the spheroplasts using a plastic transfer pipette in 12% Ficoll, 10 mM Tris-HCl, and 200 μM EDTA at a concentration of 2 ml/g-cells.
Transfer the resuspended spheroplasts to a glass homogenizer.
Gently homogenize on ice with the loose fitting pestle of the glass homogenizer for 20-30 strokes.
Transfer the lysed spheroplasts to centrifuge tubes.
Overlay the lysed spheroplasts with same volume of 12% Ficoll, 10 mM Tris-HCl, and 200 μM EDTA buffer.
Centrifuge at 4 °C at 100,000 x g for 1.5 hours in an SW28 rotor or equivalent.
Gently transfer the top floating white layer to a new centrifuge tube(s) using either a pipettor or a bent Pasteur pipette.
Add enough volume of 12% Ficoll, 10 mM Tris-HCl, and 200 μM EDTA buffer to the sample so that it fills roughly one-third of the centrifuge tube.
Add the equivalent volume of 8% Ficoll, 10 mM Tris-HCl, and 200 μM EDTA buffer to the top of the sample(s) in the new centrifuge tube(s).
Centrifuge at 4 °C at 100,000 x g for 1 hour in an SW28 rotor or equivalent.
Gently transfer the top floating white layer to a new centrifuge tube(s) using either a pipettor or a bent Pasteur pipette.
Add 600 mM sorbitol, 8% Ficoll, 10 mM Tris-HCl, and 200 μM EDTA buffer to fill about one-third of the centrifuge tube.
Add the equivalent volume of 250 mM sorbitol, 10 mM Tris-HCl, and 200 μM EDTA buffer to the top of the sample(s).
Centrifuge at 4 °C at 100,000 x g for 1 hour in an SW28 rotor or equivalent.
Transfer the top white layer, which should contain only lipid droplets and bound proteins, to dialysis tubing.
Dialyze overnight into 10 mM Tris-HCl and 200 μM EDTA buffer to eliminate the Ficoll.
Dissolve 9 g NaCl in dH2O to yield a 1 L solution for NaCl preparation.
Filter sterilize the NaCl solution using a 0.2 μm membrane.
Prepare 10x HBSS by dissolving each of KCl, KH2PO4, NaCl, D-glucose in dH2O and mixing them together.
Filter sterilize the 10x HBSS using a 0.2 μm membrane.
Combine 70 ml 10x HBSS with 3.3 ml 7.5% Na Bicarbonate, 17.5 ml 1 M HEPES, and 266.1 ml dH2O to prepare enzyme digestion buffer.
Filter sterilize the enzyme digestion buffer using a 0.2 μm membrane.
Store the enzyme digestion buffer at 4°C.
Add 5 ml sterile 0.9% NaCl to a vial of DNase just before use and keep on ice until use or store at -20°C.
Obtain a human placenta and process as close to the time of delivery as possible.
Transport the placenta in a sealed vessel such as a cooler.
Transfer the placenta to a sterile autoclavable container in a biological safety hood.
Wash blood from placenta and membranes using sterile 0.9% NaCl solution.
Discard bloody saline in a 1 L beaker as liquid biological waste.
Place the placenta on a sterile field with the smooth surface up.
Remove fetal membranes and umbilical cord with sharp, fine-point scissors and forceps.
Flip the placenta over so that the maternal surface is facing up.
Remove basal plate tissue about 3 mm from the surface.
Dissect one cotyledon at a time avoiding the chorionic plate.
Collect villous tissue into a 250 ml beaker with saline.
Rinse tissue several times in a separate beaker with 0.9% NaCl, using the 1 L beaker for liquid waste.
Transfer one cotyledon at a time to a 150 mm Petri dish.
Hold the tissue with forceps and scrape from vessels on the Petri dish.
Place scraped tissue into a separate beaker containing 0.9% NaCl.
Repeat scraping and rinsing steps for all tissue pieces.
Transfer small portions of the tissue to a cell dissociation sieve and rinse extensively with 0.9% NaCl until eluate is clear.
Repeat rinsing step for all tissue pieces.
Rinse scraped tissue in the cell dissociation sieve.
Drain excess liquid from the rinsed tissue and weigh it.
Store the weighed tissue overnight at 4 °C in a sterile Erlenmeyer flask containing DMEM.
Prepare the tissue digestion mixture by combining 100 ml of prewarmed enzyme dilution buffer, 1 ml DNase I, and 20 ml of 2.5% trypsin.
Transfer 60 g of tissue to a 500 ml sterile Erlenmeyer flask.
Add the tissue digestion mixture to the flask containing the tissue.
Incubate at 37 °C in a shaker for 45 min at 150 rpm.
Set the digestion flask at a tilt until undissociated tissue settles.
Collect the supernatant, taking care not to collect undissociated tissue.
Add an equal amount of HBSS to the collected supernatant and transfer into sterile 15 ml centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the homogenate at 4 °C at 1,000 x g for 15 min.
Aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the pellet after centrifugation.
Transfer the villous cells (white portion of the pellet) to a sterile 50 ml conical centrifuge tube and keep on ice.
Filter the cell suspension using a 100 μm Nylon cell strainer into a sterile 50 ml conical centrifuge tube.
If filtration slows, lift upward on the filter to draw a vacuum within the tube.
Centrifuge at 4 °C at 1,000 x g for 10 min.
Carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Prepare 50 ml of Hypotonic Lysis Medium (HLM) containing 20 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.4 and 1 mM EDTA.
Add protease inhibitors to HLM just before use.
Resuspend the cell pellet in ice-cold HLM at a ratio of 4 times the volume of the cell pellet using a 10 ml pipette.
Incubate the resuspended cells on ice for 10 min.
Transfer the suspended cells to a Dounce homogenizer that is kept on ice.
Homogenize the cells by applying 20-25 gentle strokes with the loose-fitting pestle of the homogenizer.
Centrifuge the cell lysate at 4 °C at 3,000 x g for 10 min to remove unbroken cells and debris.
Collect the supernatant and transfer it to a SW28 tube or an alternative tube suitable for centrifugation at 25,000 x g.
Centrifuge the collected supernatant at 4 °C at 25,000 x g for 20 min to remove mitochondria.
Prepare 50 ml of 100 mM sodium carbonate buffer (pH 11.5).
Prepare 50 ml of 60% sucrose solution.
Add protease inhibitors to the sodium carbonate buffer just before use.
Collect supernatant from step 2.6 into a 50 ml centrifuge tube.
Adjust collected supernatant to 20% sucrose.
Transfer adjusted supernatant into the bottom of an ultracentrifuge tube for an SW28 rotor.
Overlay density-adjusted supernatant with about 10 ml ice-cold sodium carbonate buffer (pH 11.5).
Add approximately 0.5-1 ml ice-cold HLM to fill the tube.
Centrifuge at 4 °C at 130,000 x g for 45 min using SW28 rotor.
Allow rotor to coast to a stop with zero deceleration.
Collect floating layer from centrifuged sample.
Adjust collected floating layer to 10% sucrose.
Transfer adjusted floating layer into the bottom of a 13.2 ml ultracentrifuge tube for an SW41Ti rotor.
Overlay density-adjusted floating layer with about 5 ml ice-cold sodium carbonate buffer (pH 11.5).
Add approximately 0.5 ml ice-cold HLM to fill the tube.
Centrifuge at 4 °C at 274,000 x g for 60 min using SW41Ti rotor.
Allow rotor to coast to a stop with zero deceleration.
Carefully collect top floating layer containing lipid droplets with a 1 ml pipette.
Repeat step of collecting and centrifuging the top floating layer at 274,000 x g for 30 min using SW41Ti rotor.
Carefully collect the top white-colored floating layer containing lipid droplets with a bent Pasteur pipette into three 1.5 ml tubes containing 100 μl HLM.
